subject: ent
title: Neck masses and neck dissection

steps.tx: The neck divides by sternomastoid into **anterior and posterior triangles**, further split by digastric, omohyoid and midline strap landmarks. Age rules the differential: children grow congenital and inflammatory lumps, young adults add lymphoma and salivary disease, older adults carry metastatic nodes until proven otherwise. The 80 percent rule warns that most non thyroid neck masses in adults are neoplastic and most of those are metastatic. Any supraclavicular node hunts primaries below the clavicles (lung, breast, abdomen via thoracic duct on the left).
steps.say: Old neck lump is cancer until biopsies say otherwise. Left neck node above collarbone looks below the diaphragm.

steps.tx: Congenital midline and lateral cysts declare by movement and site: **thyroglossal duct cysts** rise on tongue protrusion and swallowing (tract to foramen caecum, Sistrunk operation removes cyst plus hyoid body and tract core to prevent recurrence), while **branchial (second cleft) cysts** swell at the anterior border of upper sternomastoid, fluctuant and transilluminant, excised completely after infection settles. Cystic hygroma (lymphangioma) infiltrates infant neck diffusely with brilliantly transilluminant multiloculation. Midline dermoids sit but do not move with tongue, separating them from thyroglossal remnants.
steps.say: Moves with tongue out: thyroglossal, take hyoid with it. Upper neck cyst at jaw angle in young adult: second cleft.

steps.tx: Workup of an adult neck mass refuses open biopsy first: full upper aerodigestive examination (nasopharynx, tonsil, tongue base, larynx) plus **fine needle aspiration** of the node, with ultrasound guidance and HPV, EBV and thyroglobulin adjuncts. Unknown primary protocol images neck and chest then examines under anaesthesia with directed biopsies and tonsillectomy or tongue base mucosectomy in selected cases. Open neck biopsy before the primary is found seeds skin, distorts planes and ruins dissection options, reserved for lymphoma suspicion when needles fail.
steps.say: Scope the throat, needle the node, never cut the neck open first. Unknown primary hides in tonsil or tongue base.

steps.tx: Nodal **levels I to VI** map dissection: I submental and submandibular, II to IV jugular chain high to low, V posterior triangle, VI central compartment, VII superior mediastinum. **Radical neck dissection** sacrifices sternomastoid, internal jugular and accessory nerve; modified radical preserves one or more; **selective dissection** (e.g. supraomohyoid I to III for oral cavity) samples at risk basins. Shoulder syndrome follows accessory nerve loss (trapezius droop, cannot abduct past ninety degrees). Postoperative chyle leak (left level IV milky drain, triglyceride rich) needs pressure, diet modification and occasionally thoracic duct ligation.
steps.say: Levels map the knife. Keep the nerve to keep the shoulder. Milky left drain is chyle from thoracic duct.
